item.title: CVE-2026-133001 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 5.3
item.description:
Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 5.3 | FlowIntel contains an authorization flaw in its duplicate alert ingestion logic. When a duplicate alert is received and its content is updated, the ownership and visibility scope fields (owner user and owner organization) were not refreshed to reflect the connector's current scope. As a result, an alert that was originally created under a broader visibility scope retained that broader scope even after the connector's scope was narrowed or changed.
This means that users or organizations that should no longer have visibility into a given alert could continue to access it, because the stale ownership fields were never updated during the duplicate-update path. The issue affected all duplicate updates, including those involving alerts in terminal review states and those recovered from uniqueness conflicts.
Security impact: - Unauthorized disclosure of security alert content to users or organizations outside the intended visibility scope. - Stale access persists indefinitely until the alert is independently re-scoped or deleted.
Affected version: <4.1.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-82948 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 7.1
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 7.1 | The Guardian 2 alarm unit lacks a mechanism to authenticate control commands sent over 433.92 MHz, which allows an attacker to replay the static commands to impersonate activity. The attacker can also disarm or arm the system at will if a Nexsmart keypad (product link) is in use, thus compromising the functionality of the alarm system completely.

item.title: CVE-2026-82949 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 7.1
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 7.1 | The static codes used for information transmission throughout the 433.92 MHz system of the Guardian 2 system allow an attacker in proximity to monitor the movements of users inside the premises where the sensors are set up. This is further aided by the fact that codes transmitted reveal sensor type, although sensor location cannot be inferred from this traffic alone.

item.title: CVE-2026-82950 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 7.1
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 7.1 | The device only supports Wi-Fi protocols vulnerable to deauthentication attacks (WEP/WPA/WPA2). Should any event which would typically be logged to the user’s mobile device (such as arming or disarming the alarm or any tamper events) be incurred whilst the device is temporarily disconnected from its Wi-Fi network (such as via a deauthentication attack), those alerts will not be sent even after connection is regained.
